question: Can a bounded four-head anchor-to-proposal weight interpolation preserve old-public-history Brier while retaining nonzero new-event fitting on a previously consumed development trace, without hard-vetoing the entire shared update?
hypothesis: A per-head five-point interpolation will allow a positive (>0) specialist update fraction for at least three of five fixed historical samples while respecting a +0.02 original-head old-Brier ceiling; after-event observed one-witness transition Brier improves versus all-frozen-anchor heads at at least two of five samples. These are only source-consumed in-sample diagnostics, not held scientific claims.

inputs.name: original-consumed-P0-joint-checkpoint
inputs.source: original existing P0 Actions archive; P0 parent source already seen

inputs.name: original-P0-public-ledger
inputs.source: original 1025 prior witnessed source actions; previously consumed

inputs.name: original-existing-A-B-A-suffix-96
inputs.source: already consumed existing selection-dev-01 trace; exact SHA validated by original pinned producer.json at repository source

frozen_design.split: retrospective old 1025 public witnessed rows for constraint and previously consumed individual post-update row for observed fit; no new held-out split or first-use; no prospective scientific inference
frozen_design.ordering: only exact sampled ordinals; one original unmodified 96-event replay, no guard enforcement
frozen_design.data_budget: 0 new world actions, 0 new hidden data, only source-pinned archived original consumed rows
frozen_design.compute_budget: at most 5 alpha values × 4 heads × 1025 old-row Brier predictions per sampled ordinal, plus 3 × 4 new-row diagnostic predictions; no optimization search outside these values
frozen_design.capacity: same four native JEPA head matrix dimensions and existing retained anchor weights; zero extra active specialists; research sidecar only; no canonical checkpoint restoration/promotion

controls: alpha=0 anchor-only per-head specialist memory freeze
alpha=1 unguarded proposed four-head one-step update
original existing G23 hard veto of all state when any head exceeds 0.02
negative controls wrong head identity, forged ledger prefix, >1 new witness, modified checkpoint, bad head output or mutation, no new source action
metrics: per selected ordinal/head chosen alpha, old Brier delta relative to P0 old head and observed post-fit new witness Brier
number of samples with any positive transition alpha
number of samples in which repaired transition mean Brier on just-consumed witness improves over all-frozen old-head prediction
number of heads within original +0.02 bound and whole-update hard-veto comparison
original model and proposed checkpoint SHA unchanged, source action count 0, no cold owner restore

classification_rules.supported: DEV_MECHANISM_PROMISING only if all 4 selected adjusted heads stay <= +0.02 original old-task Brier, at least 3/5 samples have positive alpha on at least one transition specialist, and >=2/5 sampled after-fit observed transition loss improves vs all-frozen P0 heads. Never a SCIENTIFIC_PASS.
classification_rules.mixed: All constraints hold but fewer than all prereg positive-progress criteria; emit DEV_MIXED_NO_GO, no retuning.
classification_rules.negative: Any source-valid sample violates an old-head bound, or all progress metrics fail; emit DEV_NO_GO while preserving genuine negative.
classification_rules.invalid: Any source/trace pin mismatch, altered historical prefix, changed original source state, invalid head weights/shape, missing checkpoint custody, test or full regression failure; infrastructure/test failures separate from science.

prohibited_after_primary_run: promoting headwise sidecar to canonical model
preregistration_note: Preregistration committed BEFORE scoring this newly proposed mechanism. Prior G24 outcomes on the same consumed sample are already visible: this is exploratory DEV-only test; cannot claim independent prospective science. Model weight blending is not source-equivalent to official NativeCausalAmalgam.restore; requires separate future owner-qualified checkpoint contract.
